text:
Connor Bedard has spent the week answering questions about his coach, and that tells you where the Blackhawks are. After six straight losses, Bedard publicly backed Jeff Blashill, and the commentary that followed has been less about whether Chicago is improving than about whether anyone can fix it.

The record is 5-13-2 with 12 points, and the underlying numbers don't argue. Chicago has taken 42% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), allows 3.58 expected goals per 60 minutes, and has given up 82 goals in 20 games, nearly ten more than its chances would usually allow. Our playoff odds round to zero.

The goaltending has been the sharpest wound. Spencer Knight is at .844 and 5.1 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and Arvid Soderblom cleared waivers and went to Rockford, where he posted a shutout. The young defense pair of Wyatt Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov has been outscored 15-4.

There's still a reason to watch. Bedard with Tyler Bertuzzi and rookie Roman Kantserov, who extended a point streak to eight games, is the line with the most upside, even if it's losing its minutes for now. Anton Frondell is getting looks too. For this season, the story is the kids, and whether the losing changes the room.
